title: Review Animal Services field-call records
creation_date_basis: Estimated from the November 2 receipt of records; this task first appears in Git on November 3.
instructions: Review the records received in response to the October 20 Stockton Animal Services field-call request. Preserve the original files and receipt details, document the date range, fields, definitions, coverage, missing or redacted information, and limitations. Analyze patterns relevant to where dogs need help and what happens after reports; distinguish administrative records from firsthand observations and do not treat calls as unique dogs or verified street population. Record findings and next actions only after reviewing the evidence.

list_context: Nov 2 field observation · Count visible dogs across a limited area
title: Verify conditions: scale of the dog problem near St. Mary's
creation_date_basis: Estimated from the first Git record on October 31; the task may have been planned earlier.
instructions: On November 2, 2026, observe a manageable portion of the St. Mary's–Church Street corridor from public areas to establish an initial firsthand picture of approximately how many dogs are visible and how widely they are distributed. Record the date, the general area actually examined, an approximate dog count including zero if none are seen, basic observed circumstances, and limits of the observation. This is not a complete census. Do not enter St. Mary's Community Services to interview staff. Do not assume dogs living with people are abandoned or publish identifying details about residents or sensitive animal locations.

list_context: Identify a supported public location first
title: Verify reported conditions in South Stockton / District 5
creation_date_basis: Estimated from the first Git record on October 29; the task may have been planned earlier.
instructions: Use the generalized Carrie Street levee area in Weston Ranch as a specific historical lead: Stocktonia reported an April 23, 2026 roaming-dog attack near the 800 block, while KCRA's separate September account described increased stray- and dumped-dog encounters across District 5 without naming a site. Choose a safe public observation route near the reported Carrie Street area, confirm access and current conditions before visiting, and document what is actually present, including zero dogs if none are seen. Do not treat the April incident as evidence of current danger or assume the September encounters occurred there. Distinguish both published reports from firsthand findings and record follow-up questions.

list_context: Clarify field access and current care needs
title: Follow up with Stockton Street Dogs
creation_date_basis: Estimated from the first Git record on October 27; the task may have been planned earlier.
instructions: Check whether the October 7 volunteer application received a response. Ask for the current status and evidence of progress on Canine Campus, and identify practical approved volunteer or care opportunities, requirements, schedules, and contacts. Record any reply only when received.
checklist: What is the current status of Canine Campus?
What are the next milestones and obstacles?
What other major developments are underway?
What help is most needed right now?
Are there specific approved tasks with a location, schedule, supplies, and participation requirements?
If five new volunteers were available tomorrow, what could they actually do?
What coordination problems prevent willing people from helping?
Do you coordinate feeding or water, and can residents join an established route?
What supplies are useful, where should they be delivered, and who handles veterinary referrals?

list_context: Clarify reported locations and seek firsthand leads
title: Contact CBS reporter Charlie Lapastora
creation_date_basis: Estimated from the first Git record on October 28; the task may have been planned earlier.
instructions: Follow up on the April 6 and June 8 CBS Sacramento reports about abandoned dogs in Stockton. Ask what evidence was gathered, what has happened since, and whether the reporter can connect Crossover with firsthand observers with their permission. Record contact or answers only if they actually occur.
checklist: Isabel Guzman was reportedly documenting abandoned dogs near Stanislaus Street for over a year. What was she documenting, and could you introduce us with her permission?
Did your reporting identify specific areas where dogs were regularly found, beyond the general locations mentioned in the articles?
What happened to the dogs featured in your April report? Were they rescued, reunited, or otherwise helped?
How were the estimates of 200–400 street dogs established? Is there underlying documentation?
Have you learned anything new about the situation, the rescue efforts, or the proposed Safe Grounds project since your reports?
